title: Chain side effects left to right with andThen

blocks.text: `Consumer.andThen(after)` builds a consumer that runs `this` first and `after` second, handing **both the same input**. Chaining is how a pipeline of side effects (log, then store, then notify) is put together from small steps.
Write `ConsumerChain.chain(List<Consumer<T>> steps)`. It returns one `Consumer<T>` that, on `accept(t)`, runs every step in list order on `t`.
The list may contain `null` entries and may be empty; the returned consumer must be usable either way. Think about what should happen to the remaining steps when one of them throws.

cases.says: Every step runs, first to last, and each one receives the same input.
A null step is left out of the chain; andThen(null) would throw.
With no steps the chain is still a consumer, one that does nothing.
When a step throws, the exception reaches the caller and the later steps do not run.

concepts: andThen runs the first consumer and then the second, handing both the same input.
When a consumer in an andThen chain throws, the steps after it do not run.
